blocking_question: (1) does any .atlas structure need rkyv-style self-relative pointers given file-start absolute offsets with bounds/overlap rules? (2) the conditional exception -- rkyv as a real Cargo dependency for an internal cache -- had no consumer

measurement.relative_pointers: .atlas wire v1 records are flat and length-delimited; the section directory addresses payloads by absolute offsets from the file start with bounds checks and overlap rejection (ATLAS-BINARY-WIRE-FORMAT.md, G64 reader), which is already position-independent under mmap; no record points into another, so there is nothing for a self-relative pointer to address
measurement.cache_consumer: the consumer now exists: ADR 0008's per-artifact extraction cache, keyed on content digest, extractor identity and build digest (96/96 hits on a warm run, G80). Its JSON encoding: 96 entries, 96 MB, 73,174 observations, fully deserialized into owned ExtractionBatch values in 0.34-0.37 s (release build, 3 rounds) -- about 5% of a 7.3 s warm systemize
measurement.zero_copy_bound: zero-copy access could remove at most those ~0.35 s, and less in practice: the census pipeline consumes owned batches, so archived access would still deserialize or require rewriting every consumer
measurement.dependency_cost: rkyv plus its validation and pointer-metadata support crates would enter the production runtime to save ~0.35 s -- against the zero-runtime-dependency discipline
measurement.method: document comparison against the wire contract and reader; scratch release harness deserializing the real cache directory with the workspace's own ExtractionBatch type

finding: neither part needs rkyv: the wire has no internal pointers, and the one real cache loads fast enough from its hand-rolled (serde JSON) encoding that the conditional-dependency exception lapses
